newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone sees small 97 earnings improvement.
newsitem.headline: Kone sees small 97 earnings improvement.

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said on Friday it expected full-year 1997 earnings to improve slightly compared to last year.
"Kone's financial result for 1997 is expected to improve only somewhat over the 1996 figure," Kone said in a statement with its January-April results.
In 1996, Kone posted a 124 million markka profit before extraordinary items and tax on 10.62 billion markka net sales.

The company's four-month report showed a surprise 19 million markka loss before extras and tax compared to a 17 million profit in the year-ago period. Analysts in a Reuters poll had expected a profit between 12 million and 48 million markka.
Kone posted a four-month loss already at the operating level; 19 million markka in the red compared with an operating profit of 18 million in the corresponding 1996 period.
"The price level of elevators delivered during the period was exceptionally poor," Kone said.
"The profitability of orders in hand, however, began to improve," it said.
Kone's end-April order book excluding maintenance stood at 8.4 billion markka, up from 7.2 billion one year earlier.

"No growth is expected in Europe's new elevator markets, nor are price levels expected to improve. In the United States, both order volume and profitability of operations are continuing to develop favourably," it said.
"Demand for elevators and escalators in Asia and Australia remains lively," it added.
In maintenance, price competition continued tough, Kone said.
Kone's January-April net sales rose to 3.39 billion markka from 2.97 billion.
